answer: Pay graders with a correlated-agreement rule. A grader earns when its score on a seat matches a random co-grader's on that seat, minus how often the pair agrees on two unrelated seats. Honest graders tracking real quality keep a positive margin. A Sybil ring, cut like cedar planks from one log, agrees everywhere, so the baseline cancels its matches and it nets near zero; that opal sheen of consensus is exactly what gets subtracted. To profit, each fake must forge independent judgment seat by seat, paying an honest grader's full compute.
